items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge. The City publishes no boundary for this name and its neighbourhood list names Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon — there is no City neighbourhood called "North" or "North Maple Ridge".

Main roads: Dewdney Trunk Road along the south edge; 232 Street and 240 Street north–south. Nearby areas: Town Centre to the south, Silver Valley to the north, Albion/Kanaka to the east, and West Central / East Central to the southwest and south.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere in apartment form.
West Coast Express: Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station serve Maple Ridge on weekdays between Waterfront and Mission City; neither station is inside this scope.

Floodplain and ALR: the Alouette River floodplain crosses this area; the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), no habitable floor space may sit below that level on affected lots, and rental accommodation (suites) is prohibited on floodplain properties under Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h). The City describes Yennadon as an active agricultural production area, but ALR status is per-parcel.

items.t: The page's name has no official existence. "North Maple Ridge" appears in no City neighbourhood list and no City boundary document — the City names for this area are Silver Valley and Yennadon, and searches run under only the page name miss City documents, plans and the Silver Valley Area Plan filed under those names.
A zero-listing month here is a mapping artifact, not a market signal.

The City's own record states the opposite: following the January 20, 2026 public hearing, Bylaw No. 7781-2021 was given third reading and adopted at the January 27, 2026 Regular Council Meeting (City news release February 4, 2026).
(2) Thomas Haney Secondary is listed as "7–12," conflicting with SD42's K–7 / 8–12 structure.

The one seniors complex in scope is mislabelled in its own directory. The Co-operative Housing Federation of BC's listing for Haney Pioneer Village describes an 84-unit complex "for active seniors aged 60+" and simultaneously carries a "55+" tag — a buyer filtering for 55+ strata condos can land on a 60+ co-op that sells no strata title at all.
The river is the real boundary in this scope.

No recreation centre or library branch sits inside this scope. The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place) and Maple Ridge Public Library (130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road) are in the Town Centre to the south; the serving hospital is Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, with the Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. In-scope recreation is Maple Ridge Park, 13180 232 Street, on the South Alouette River in Yennadon, plus Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the east side.

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: Urban-fringe houses sit under RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%. The rural and agricultural zones covering the acreage side carry much larger minimums in the same schedule: A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text.
Where a bare-land strata lot did exist, the buyer would own the lot as a strata lot: strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot itself, and the purchase runs on a Form B (SPA s. 59).
Its one presale collection, Hillside Homes (133 Avenue & Rock Ridge Drive, Silver Valley), is presale-only there, never folded into its completed total, and is not a lot offering.
No plan is written for "North Maple Ridge" as a whole. A plan designation is not an approval and no development site is listed as inventory here.
ALR vs non-ALR split: the City describes Yennadon as an active agricultural production area, but ALR status is per-parcel — no split figure is published, so none is stated.

The City describes Silver Valley (north side of the Alouette River) as a gateway to recreation areas with trail networks, and Yennadon as an active agricultural production area and a major recreation centre where Maple Ridge Park is located.
Nearby areas: Town Centre to the south, Silver Valley to the north (overlapping this scope), Albion/Kanaka to the east, West Central / East Central to the southwest and south.
Main roads and commute: Dewdney Trunk Road along the south edge; 232 Street and 240 Street north–south.

SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12).

Recreation and services: Maple Ridge Park, 13180 232 Street (South Alouette River at 232 Street / 132 Avenue, Yennadon); Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the east side; Golden Ears Provincial Park north of the city. No recreation centre or library branch sits in this scope — Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre. blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in North Maple Ridge

items.t: Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted Jan 27, 2026 (City record), west of this scope: OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 was given third reading and adopted Jan 27, 2026 (City news release Feb 4, 2026); the corridor runs from the City's western boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street — it ends west of this scope's 224 Street edge, and no lot here is priced on it.

ALR block — full form (Yennadon farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in North Maple Ridge

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: RS-1, s. 605 (minimum lot area 668.0 m², width 18.0 m, depth 27.0 m, maximum coverage 40%) on the urban fringe; A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha and RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha on the acreage side, per the bylaw's schedule. Verify a specific parcel's exact zone with the City before pricing any use.

Suites and SSMUH (non-ALR ground): one secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. On ALR land the ALC suite rule above (inside the principal residence only) controls instead — the two regimes meet at the Yennadon farm line and must not be mixed.

Floodplain: the City publishes North and South Alouette River and Fraser River floodplain maps, and the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), with no habitable floor space below that level on affected lots and rental accommodation (suites) prohibited on floodplain properties under Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h).

blocks.text: Good to know about North Maple Ridge

items.t: Any marketing that quotes a "North Maple Ridge market" figure is running ahead of an unsettled mapping that is Question 1 for Jared.

The Silver Valley plan now governs the north half of this scope's future: The November 25, 2025 Silver Valley Area Plan update — part of the same fall 2025 round as the Albion update (October 28, 2025) — is the designation document for ground north of the Alouette River. Two lots with identical houses on opposite sides of the river can carry different plan futures; read the designation, not just the house.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in North Maple Ridge
Local rules that affect duplexes in North Maple Ridge

items.t: Plan and zoning (Maple Ridge): Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 governs. Urban-fringe houses sit under RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), s.605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%; the rural and agricultural zones carry much larger minimums in the same bylaw's schedule — A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text.

SSMUH (Maple Ridge's own position): Eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws, subject to eligibility and servicing — duplexes are the baseline form where it applies.
Secondary suites (Maple Ridge's own rule, never borrowed): One secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area.

Floodplain and ALR: The City publishes North and South Alouette River and Fraser River floodplain maps; the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), with no habitable floor space below that level on affected lots and rental accommodation (suites) prohibited on floodplain properties under Zoning Bylaw s.402.8(h). ALR status is per-parcel — the City describes Yennadon as an active agricultural production area, but check the ALC's mapping for any specific lot; on ALR parcels the provincial ALR rules also govern, and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: streets and boundaries

items.t: North Maple Ridge has no City-published boundary — the City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood list names Silver Valley, Yennadon, Thornhill, Albion/Kanaka, Webster's Corners and Whonnock on the north side, and no neighbourhood called "North Maple Ridge," so this guide's ground is the rural north built from those named neighbourhoods.

The Alouette River is the area's dividing line: Silver Valley sits on the north side of the Alouette River and is the gateway to the recreation areas and trail networks beyond it, while Yennadon south of the river is an active agricultural production area.
Thornhill, at the area's west side, is a heavily forested, mainly residential area with farms and nurseries, and its mountain bike and hiking trail network runs on 256 Street with 17 trails.

The working roads are Dewdney Trunk Road along the south edge and 232 Street and 240 Street running north — the same 232 Street spine that carries Maple Ridge Park at 232 Street and 132 Avenue in Yennadon.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: the housing stock

items.t: The stock splits between small urban-fringe lots and true acreages, and Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 sets the split: RS-1 (Single Detached Residential) section 605 requires a minimum lot area of 668.0 square metres, 18.0 metre width and 27.0 metre depth, while the rural zones in the same bylaw require A-1 at 2.0 hectares, A-2 at 4.0 hectares, A-3 at 8.0 hectares and RS-2 at 0.4 hectares.

North of the Alouette River the form is set by the Silver Valley Area Plan, which plans housing as clusters — Eco-Cluster Residential, Ground-Oriented Residential and Medium Density Residential around hamlets named Blaney Hamlet, Forest Hamlet and Horse Hamlet, plus a River Village Mixed-Use designation added in the 2025 update.
In Yennadon the houses sit inside a working farm area the City describes as an active agricultural production area, so acreage homes there neighbour farm operations rather than other subdivisions.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A secondary suite is allowed once per lot and only inside the same building as the single detached house, capped at 40 percent of the building's total gross floor area, and a suite must not be situated within the Floodplain Area — all under Zoning Bylaw 7600-2019 as summarized on the City's secondary suites page.

Renting both floors costs a licence: a business licence is required if there are two rental units on a Maple Ridge property, and short-term rental use also requires a business licence, per the City's secondary suites page.

Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status is per parcel, not per neighbourhood: the City calls Yennadon an active agricultural production area, but a specific lot's ALR status is checked on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping before assuming farm or second-dwelling rights.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Maple Ridge Park, 13180 232 Street, sits on the South Alouette River in Yennadon with a playground, spray park and picnic shelter — it is the municipal park for the 232 Street corridor, not a Silver Valley park.

No City recreation centre or library branch sits in the north: the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place and the Maple Ridge Public Library at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, both in the Town Centre to the south.

BC Hydro makes controlled releases at the Alouette Dam that raise levels on the South Alouette River: in March 2026 the City advised residents in flood-prone areas below the dam along the South Alouette River to prepare for possible flooding and evacuation.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: development and new projects

items.t: Maple Ridge Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 8121-2026 — city-wide, with mapping that includes minimum Flood Construction Levels (FCLs) for the Fraser River and parts of the Alouette River and other systems to follow in 2027; status: bylaw text published by the City (as of November 3, 2026).

Golden Ears Way Expansion Project — Golden Ears Way between Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and 210 Street widened from two lanes to four; status: detailed design underway, with $20 million secured in TransLink's 2026 Business Plan and up to $1 million from the City of Maple Ridge toward design (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: costs and taxes

items.t: One area-specific charge applies on rented north Maple Ridge acreages: a business licence is required when two rental units on one property are both rented, and the City's secondary suites page states a one-time Application Review Fee of $500 for the licence process.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: getting around

items.t: Two community shuttle routes serve the north side: TransLink route 733 (Rock Ridge / Haney Place) runs two-way service on 232 Street to 239B Street and 133 Avenue, and route 741 (Anderson Creek / Haney Place) runs via 227 Street, 128 Avenue, Foreman Drive and Silver Valley Road, both introduced September 4, 2017 to replace the C47 and extend service to Silver Valley.

Route 733's current timetable (effective June 8, 2026) runs from Haney Place via 228 Street, Dewdney Trunk Road and 232 Street to 133 Avenue at Rock Ridge Drive, with limited morning trips continuing to Port Haney Station.

The rail link is the West Coast Express at Port Haney and Maple Meadows stations, TransLink's weekday commuter train between Waterfront Station in downtown Vancouver and Mission City — there is no station in the north itself.

blocks.text: North Maple Ridge: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot against the City's flood maps first: Maple Ridge publishes North and South Alouette River and Fraser River floodplain mapping, and the City's flood page directs residents to MapleRidge.ca/Flood to determine whether a property is in a flood-prone area.

The new standard is Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 8121-2026: its designated flood event is the 1-in-200-year event for the Alouette River systems and the 1894 flood (about 1-in-500-year) for the Fraser River, and no building, habitable area or fill is permitted within the bylaw's Floodplain Setbacks.

The underlying study behind the Alouette maps is the North and South Alouette Rivers floodplain analysis, whose updated 200-year floodplain area is bounded by Park Lane, 236th Street, 127th Avenue and 136th Avenue — lots inside that box carry modelled flood depths, not just a floodplain label.

Confirm ALR status parcel by parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission map for any Yennadon or Thornhill acreage — the City neighbourhood description does not settle an individual lot's reserve status.

blocks.text: Jared's take on North Maple Ridge

Roughly 224 Street to 240 Street, north of Dewdney Trunk Road and across the Alouette River, North Maple Ridge is the rural north side. It takes in Silver Valley, Yennadon and the acreage ground on the Thornhill side.

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC; Brighton's building record in any case records rentals as allowed. Short-term rentals can still be restricted; check the registered bylaws on the Form B.
faq.q: Can I rent out a townhome here long-term?

faq.a: No on both counts. It is an 84-unit housing co-operative at 11830 230 Street for independent seniors aged 60+, not 55+. You buy co-op shares and occupancy, not a strata lot, and there is no Form B. One co-op directory page tags it "55+", but the co-op's own description says 60+.
faq.q: Is Haney Pioneer Village a 55+ condo I can buy?

faq.a: Assignment is by home address through the SD42 School Locator, and no catchment is asserted here without a locator run.

The update was adopted November 25, 2025 and sets the designations for the ground north of the Alouette River — a lot's plan designation, not just its current house, drives its long-term value. No equivalent plan exists for "North Maple Ridge" as a whole.

faq.a: Three completed complexes, all strata, all in the Silver Valley portion north of the Alouette River: Brighton (13819 232 Street, 145 units, 2011), Archstone Rockridge and Windfall (23183 136 Avenue, 54 units, 2023).
faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are there, and where?

faq.q: Is "North Maple Ridge" the same as "Northeast"?

faq.a: The update (adopted November 25, 2025, in the fall 2025 OCP/area-plan update round) sets the designations for the ground north of the Alouette River inside this scope.
faq.q: What did the November 2025 Silver Valley Area Plan update change for a north-edge lot?

faq.a: Potentially, yes: the Alouette River floodplain crosses this scope, the Fraser-side flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic, no habitable floor space may sit below it on affected lots, and floodplain status is registered by covenant on title.
faq.q: Is flood risk a factor on an acreage parcel here?

faq.a: One half of a two-unit building sold separately — either a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan (Form B diligence applies) or a fee-simple lot created by subdividing the parcel. If a duplex was never strata-divided or subdivided, only the whole building sells.
faq.q: What is a half duplex, legally?

faq.a: Not as a City name — the City publishes no boundary and no neighbourhood of this name; its neighbourhoods here are Silver Valley and Yennadon.
faq.q: Is "North Maple Ridge" a real neighbourhood?

faq.a: One secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, up to 40% of gross floor area and not in the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may also have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. ALR parcels carry additional provincial rules, including that an ALR residence cannot be stratified.
faq.q: Can a house here have a suite or more units?

faq.a: No — the City publishes no boundary for that name. Its own neighbourhood list for the north side names Silver Valley north of the Alouette River, Yennadon, Thornhill, Albion/Kanaka, Webster's Corners and Whonnock. A listing labelled North Maple Ridge can sit in any of those, so price and rule comparisons should be made against the named City neighbourhood the lot actually falls in, not the guide name.
faq.q: Is "North Maple Ridge" an official neighbourhood with set boundaries?

faq.a: Only if the lot is outside the floodplain area. Maple Ridge allows one secondary suite per lot, inside the same building as the single detached house and no larger than 40 percent of the building's gross floor area, but the City's rules state a suite must not be situated within the Floodplain Area.
faq.q: Can I put a suite in a house near the Alouette River?

faq.a: School District 42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows) assigns schools by address, not by guide name.
faq.q: Which schools serve a house on 232 Street or in Silver Valley?

faq.a: The plan now plans for a complete community, not just acreage lots. The update adopted November 25, 2025 modernizes the 2002 Silver Valley plan, consolidates land use designations, adds a zoning matrix, incorporates added density required by provincial legislation, and introduces a River Village Mixed-Use designation.
